issues.description: PR conflates three unrelated changes under a 'add POST tests' title.
issues.detail: The diff bundles new POST tests, a sweeping README reformat (handle() signature reorder, code_to_http_status swap, bounded_stream change), and a new FAQ entry. Reviewers cannot audit correctness when semantic changes hide inside cosmetic reformatting. Split into separate PRs so each change can be justified on its own.

issues.description: req.stream to req.bounded_stream swap is unexplained and contradicts the PR description.
issues.detail: The PR description says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the diff swaps to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different preconditions under WSGI when Content-Length is wrong or absent. This is the semantic change that makes the new 400 test pass, yet it gets one line and no justification. Name it, document why bounded_stream is correct.

issues.description: FAQ example handler uses nested if/else where flat structure would teach the lesson better.
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post nests selection three deep to demonstrate header setting in tests. The lesson is buried under Content-Length handling and a conditional read. Either flatten to three guarded returns or strip to the smallest handler that demonstrates the point. FAQ code gets copied; teach the idiom you want imitated.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert, a known Python footgun.
issues.detail: assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400) reads like a function call and trains readers toward assert(x, y) which is a tuple and always truthy. Write assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400. Small fix, but FAQ code is canonical and copied.

issues.description: New test cases duplicate header dicts instead of sharing a base fixture.
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 both hardcode Authorization: custom-token and Content-Type: application/json. Pull common headers into a local dict so the meaningful difference (Content-Length: 1, empty body) is the only thing that varies per case. Smaller diff, cheaper next addition.

issues.description: New tests assert status codes without stating the invariant under test.
issues.detail: resp3 checks the happy path; resp4 checks empty body with Content-Length:1 yields 400. Neither has a comment naming the property. The 400 case only holds because of the bounded_stream change, so test and production code were modified together to converge without a written postcondition.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying test additions are reasonable but the PR is poorly scoped: it bundles tests, a sweeping README reformat with semantic changes (handle() signature, status formatting, bounded_stream swap), and a new FAQ entry under a misleading title. The req.stream to req.bounded_stream swap is the actual semantic fix making the new 400 case pass, yet it is unexplained and contradicts the PR description. The FAQ example itself has issues: nested control flow that obscures the lesson and a parenthesized assert that is a Python footgun. Recommendation: split the PR, document the bounded_stream change explicitly, simplify the FAQ example, and state the invariants the new tests verify.
